title: Laser and light painting
caption: A laser guide star and light-painted letters at the Allgäu Public Observatory, Germany
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: On a clear night in Bavaria, a laser beam shoots straight up from the Allgäu Public Observatory in Ottobeuren, Germany, while the letters ESO glow in front of the building. Staff drew them in light with their mobile phones during the long exposure. The Milky Way appears just left of the beam, and dotted aircraft tracks cross the sky above the horizon.

The occasion was the filming of an ESOcast episode about ESO's new compact laser guide star unit. A laser guide star is an artificial star made in the atmosphere. The beam makes sodium atoms in a layer 90 kilometers up glow, and adaptive optics use measurements of that point of light to undo the blurring caused by the air.

The laser is powerful, at 20 watts. To protect pilots and passengers, the Deutsche Flugsicherung, which manages German air traffic control, set up a no-fly zone around the observatory during the night-time observing hours.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure photograph by M. Kornmesser, long enough for people to draw letters in light with phones. The source gives no other camera or color details.
understand.eye: The long exposure turns moving lights, such as the phones and the aircraft, into streaks and dots that the eye would never see as a single picture.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: ESO's patented and licensed design launches the laser through a small telescope, all in one modular unit that mounts directly on a large telescope. The VLT was to receive four such units, and the concept is also key to units for the future European Extremely Large Telescope. When filmed, this unit was being tested before shipping to Paranal.
alt: A vertical laser beam rising from an observatory at night, with the letters ESO drawn in light in front of it and the Milky Way to the left.
